problem: BEV value-map methods give ambiguous, weakly discriminative target-location estimates, LLM/VLM-based methods lack spatial reasoning and lose fine-grained information, and most systems pick goals greedily, causing back-and-forth movement and inefficient search.
motivation: Zero-shot object navigation needs precise estimation of where a target is likely to be in unbounded 3D space plus efficient global decisions. The authors observe that hierarchical (scene/region/object) CLIP features combined with LLM commonsense landmarks give a fine-grained 3D prior, and that a distance-aware sequential frontier plan avoids greedy oscillation.
key_idea: Build a 3D voxel belief map of target presence from hierarchical CLIP semantics and LLM landmarks, fuse it with a visibility map into a posterior, and plan a frontier visiting order minimizing expected search distance.
insight: Both the visibility map and the sequential planner matter: removing the visibility map drops SR/SPL from 62.5/31.6 to 57.2/28.0, and removing the planner (highest posterior frontier only) drops them to 56.0/29.3 because of goal switching. Hierarchical spatial semantics contribute much more than LLM landmarks (Scene only 59.0 SR vs 62.5 with all levels; landmarks only 60.0→62.5). Object-level semantics raise SR but slightly lower SPL (31.6 vs 32.0) due to slow localized search. Failure analysis shows detector errors (48.32%) and multi-floor targets (36.78%) dominate, not exploration.
method: 3D hierarchical semantic voxel map: multi-scale image patches (k=3) get CLIP features, SAM instance counts, and depth-derived volume/density. Scene, region and object scorers pick per-pixel the most confident scale, and features are back-projected into 0.25 m voxels, keeping the highest-confidence feature per level.
Hierarchical landmark generation: GPT-4o outputs three room, region and object landmark strings with relevance probabilities (summing to 1 per level) for the target.

Belief map construction: the CLIP text embeddings of landmarks and target are compared by max cosine similarity to voxel features. The prior is b_u = sum of alpha*sim over landmarks + target similarity.

Visibility map: per-pixel detection confidence (cos^2 of horizontal/vertical angle times a distance term using an LLM-given [dmin,dmax]) gives an absence likelihood for observed voxels. Posterior = visibility likelihood × prior.

Frontier observation belief: from each frontier, ray-cast the FOV in 4 directions (0/90/180/270°), sum posterior beliefs of the voxels plus w_unobserved=0.01 per unknown voxel, and take the max over directions.

Belief-based sequential planner: choose the frontier order minimizing sum of cumulative A* distance × observation belief, solved by GPU (CuPy) simulated annealing (about 0.2 s for 10 frontiers). The first frontier is taken as the goal and replanned every step, executed with the VLFM local planner.
Target verification: Grounding DINO detects the object, GPT-4o verifies it, and SAM plus depth localize it as the final goal.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, landmarks and detection verification) + CLIP ViT-B/32 + SAM + Grounding DINO + VLFM local planner
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, camera 0.88 m high) + odometry pose
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 30°, LOOK UP/DOWN 30°, STOP

numbers.extra: 500-step budget, success radius 0.1 m as stated

results: BeliefMapNav reaches SR/SPL 61.4/30.6 on HM3D, 37.3/17.6 on MP3D and 65.2/32.1 on HSSD, all zero-shot. On HM3D it has higher SR than VLFM (52.5/30.4) and GAMap (53.1/26.0) and higher SPL than InstructNav (58.0 SR/20.9 SPL, the best previous SR), a 46.4% relative SPL gain. The HSSD gain is largest (+27.8% SR, +28.9% SPL over the best prior), while MP3D gains are marginal.
limitations: Validated only on object navigation in simulation, with no real-robot experiments
Performance limited by the open-vocabulary detector (48.32% of HM3D failures) and by the local planner in narrow areas and across floors (36.78% of failures involve targets on other floors)
MP3D gains are small due to mesh holes and low data quality
